the extent of salvageable myocardium is a powerful prognosticator in patients with acute myocardial infarctions and that it is a good surrogate for the amount of infarcted myocardium that will be salvaged by reperfusion therapy.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMR) to measure infarct size is an important tool to evaluate the efficacy of new therapies in the setting of ST-segment elevation MI (STEMI).

the extent of myocardial damage can be assessed by MRI, and that the extent of damage is an important prognostic marker for longterm outcome, independent of other prognostic variables, including left ventricular ejections fraction.

the amount of salvage that is achieved in the acute setting is a very powerful predictor of outcome, and that it may be a more important predictor than left ventricular function, which has been traditionally used as the main outcome measure in clinical trials.
